description: A graduate course in defending networks: secure architecture, protocol hardening, secure channels, detection and response at every layer from the link to inter-domain routing. Students design, harden and monitor simulated enterprise, campus and provider networks, then evaluate how well their defences hold against scripted incidents.
modelledOn: Kaufman, Perlman and Speciner, Network Security: Private Communication in a Public World
NIST SP 800-207 Zero Trust Architecture and NIST SP 800-94 Guide to Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems
IETF RFCs for TLS 1.3, DNSSEC, IPsec and RPKI
outcomes: Construct threat models for enterprise and provider networks and derive segmentation and zero-trust designs from them.
Harden link, network and routing protocols with access control, anti-spoofing, authentication and origin validation.
Configure and evaluate firewalls, intrusion detection and secure channels, reasoning about false positives and failure modes.
Design mitigations and runbooks for denial of service, botnet activity and wireless or cellular threats.
Monitor networks with packet capture, flow records and event correlation, and lead a network incident investigation.

units.title: Threat models and secure network architecture
topics: Network threat models: attacker positions, capabilities and goals
Defence in depth and security zones
Segmentation with VLANs, VRFs and micro-segmentation
Zero-trust architecture and identity-aware access
Network security policy, baselines and change control

units.title: Link and network layer protection
topics: ARP and IPv6 neighbour discovery weaknesses and their defences: dynamic ARP inspection, DHCP snooping, RA guard
Port security and 802.1X network access control
IP spoofing and ingress and egress filtering (BCP 38)
IPsec: AH, ESP, IKEv2, transport and tunnel modes
Site-to-site and remote-access VPN design
Protecting spanning tree, first-hop redundancy and the control plane

units.title: Firewalls and intrusion detection
topics: Stateless and stateful packet filtering
Rule-base design, ordering, shadowed rules and audit
Application-layer gateways, proxies and web application firewalls
Signature-based intrusion detection and rule writing
Anomaly-based detection, base rates and false-positive trade-offs
Intrusion prevention placement, fail-open versus fail-closed

units.title: TLS and secure channels
topics: TLS 1.3 handshake, key schedule and forward secrecy
Certificates, chains, revocation and certificate transparency
TLS misconfigurations and downgrade protection
Mutual TLS for service-to-service authentication
Secure shell: host keys, user keys and bastion design

units.title: DNS and routing security
topics: DNS cache poisoning and DNSSEC signing and validation
Encrypted DNS transports: privacy and enterprise visibility trade-offs
DNS firewalls and response policy zones
BGP prefix hijacks and route leaks
RPKI route-origin validation and prefix filtering
Routing protocol authentication and routing hygiene at African internet exchange points

units.title: Wireless and mobile network security
topics: WPA2 and WPA3 handshakes and their known weaknesses
Enterprise Wi-Fi with 802.1X and EAP methods
Rogue access points and wireless intrusion detection
Cellular security: SIM authentication, signalling risks and 5G improvements
Securing mobile money and USSD channels

units.title: Denial of service and botnets
topics: Volumetric, protocol and application-layer denial of service
Reflection and amplification and why anti-spoofing stops them
Mitigation: rate limiting, SYN cookies, scrubbing and anycast
Botnet architectures and command-and-control detection
Sinkholing, takedown coordination and CERT cooperation
Capacity planning and denial-of-service runbooks

units.title: Monitoring, traffic analysis and response
topics: Packet capture and flow records (NetFlow and IPFIX)
Analysing encrypted traffic from metadata and TLS client fingerprints
Event correlation in a security information and event management system
Hypothesis-driven threat hunting
Network forensics and incident response
Security evaluation of a complete network design

schedule.title: Threat models and zero-trust architecture
schedule.exercise: Write a threat model for a mobile-money agent network linking 500 rural kiosks to a data centre, then derive the security zones, trust boundaries and the five highest-priority controls.

tasks.title: Place a firewall, a DMZ and an internal zone in a small office topology and verify that only the web server is reachable from outside
Segment a hospital network into clinical, administrative, guest and device VLANs with inter-VLAN ACLs, and prove each allowed and denied flow with test pings
Redesign a flat campus network for zero trust with identity-aware access proxies, then show which lateral movement paths from a compromised laptop remain open

schedule.title: Protecting the access layer
schedule.exercise: Explain, with a packet sequence diagram, why ARP and IPv6 router advertisements can be forged on a shared segment and how dynamic ARP inspection and RA guard each stop it.

tasks.title: Inspect a capture of duplicate ARP replies on a switch segment, identify the conflicting MAC address and enable dynamic ARP inspection to block it
Configure 802.1X port authentication with a RADIUS server and a guest VLAN fallback, and verify behaviour for managed, unmanaged and unknown devices
Apply ingress and egress filtering at a small provider edge so no customer can send spoofed sources, and measure which test flows are dropped at each hop

schedule.title: IPsec, VPNs and control-plane protection
schedule.exercise: Compare IPsec transport and tunnel mode headers byte by byte for one packet and state what each mode protects and what it reveals to an observer.

tasks.title: Bring up a site-to-site IPsec tunnel between Accra and Kumasi branch routers and confirm with the packet inspector that payloads are encrypted
Design a remote-access VPN for field staff with split tunnelling rules, then justify which subnets go through the tunnel and which do not
Harden a core switch pair with root guard, BPDU guard and control-plane policing, then show the topology stays stable when a rogue switch is plugged in

schedule.title: Packet filtering and firewall policy
schedule.exercise: Audit a 40-rule firewall policy on paper: mark shadowed, redundant and overly broad rules and rewrite it into the smallest equivalent ordered set.

tasks.title: Write stateful firewall rules that allow outbound web and DNS from a LAN and only return traffic back in, then test five flows
Write a script that loads a firewall rule base, detects shadowed and redundant rules and reports the minimal reordering that preserves behaviour
Deploy a reverse proxy with a web application firewall in front of a clinic booking app and tune it until legitimate traffic passes with no blocks

schedule.title: Intrusion detection and prevention
schedule.exercise: Use Bayes' rule to show how an IDS with 99 percent detection and 1 percent false positives performs when only 1 in 10,000 flows is malicious, and propose two ways to improve precision.

tasks.title: Write a signature rule that alerts on a known malicious user-agent string and confirm it fires on the sample capture and not on normal traffic
Train a flow-feature anomaly detector on a week of baseline traffic and plot its ROC curve, choosing a threshold for an analyst budget of 20 alerts a day
Place inline and passive sensors in a branch network, choose fail-open or fail-closed for each, and defend the choices against an availability requirement

schedule.title: TLS, certificates and secure shell
schedule.exercise: Trace the TLS 1.3 key schedule from the shared secret to the traffic keys and explain why recording the session and later stealing the server key reveals nothing.

tasks.title: Inspect a server certificate chain, identify the issuer, validity period and subject alternative names, and explain why one hostname fails validation
Scan a web server's TLS configuration, disable legacy protocol versions and weak cipher suites, and confirm the improved result in a rescan
Set up mutual TLS between two internal services with a private certificate authority, then rotate a client certificate without downtime

schedule.title: Securing DNS
schedule.exercise: Explain how DNSSEC builds a chain of trust from the root to a .gh domain and what a validating resolver does when one signature has expired.

tasks.title: Turn on DNSSEC validation in a resolver and compare its answers for a correctly signed zone and a zone with a broken signature
Configure a response policy zone that blocks a list of known malicious domains and verify that clients receive the block page
Advise a bank on whether to allow encrypted DNS from staff laptops, weighing privacy, malware detection and regulatory monitoring in a scored case

schedule.title: Routing security
schedule.exercise: Study a published route leak incident and draw the AS paths before and during it, showing where filtering or origin validation would have stopped propagation.

tasks.title: Observe how a more-specific prefix announced by a neighbouring AS diverts traffic in a five-AS topology, and record the changed routing tables
Enable RPKI route-origin validation on border routers and confirm that invalid announcements are dropped while valid ones are kept
Write prefix filters, maximum-prefix limits and session authentication for every peer at a regional internet exchange and test them against a leak scenario

schedule.title: Wireless and cellular security
schedule.exercise: Compare the WPA2 four-way handshake with WPA3 SAE and explain why offline password guessing is no longer possible with SAE.

tasks.title: Configure enterprise Wi-Fi with 802.1X and certificate-based EAP for staff, and a separate isolated guest network with client isolation
Use wireless intrusion detection logs to locate a rogue access point broadcasting the corporate network name and quarantine its switch port
Lead a scored review of a mobile money USSD service, rating SIM-swap, session and agent-fraud risks and choosing controls within a fixed budget

schedule.title: Denial of service and its mitigation
schedule.exercise: Calculate the amplification factor for three reflection protocols from request and response sizes and explain why BCP 38 filtering removes the attack class.

tasks.title: Watch a simulated SYN flood fill a server's connection table, then enable SYN cookies and compare completed legitimate connections
Configure rate limits and an upstream scrubbing diversion for a news site under a simulated volumetric flood, keeping legitimate latency under 200 ms
Model the bandwidth a reflection attack can reach from open resolvers in a region, and estimate how much it falls as anti-spoofing adoption rises

schedule.title: Botnets and coordinated response
schedule.exercise: Draft a one-page denial-of-service runbook for a university portal during results week, with roles, thresholds, contacts and escalation steps.

tasks.title: Analyse DNS query logs to flag hosts making periodic queries to algorithmically generated domains, a common sign of botnet check-ins
Coordinate a botnet sinkhole operation with an ISP, the national CERT and a registrar in a scored scenario, deciding what evidence to share and when
Plan capacity and autoscaling for a public service so it absorbs ten times normal load, and price the standby capacity against expected outage cost

schedule.title: Traffic analysis and monitoring
schedule.exercise: Decide which data sources (full capture, flow records, DNS logs, proxy logs) a 2,000-user organisation should collect, with retention periods, storage cost and privacy limits under Act 843.

tasks.title: Export flow records from an edge router and list the top ten talkers and destination ports for one hour of traffic
Group TLS client fingerprints and connection metadata from encrypted flows to spot one host whose behaviour differs from the managed laptop fleet
Write correlation rules that join firewall, DNS and authentication events into one alert for a likely compromised account, and measure alert volume

schedule.title: Threat hunting, forensics and design review
schedule.exercise: Present a security evaluation of your own network design from the semester: threat model, controls per layer, residual risks and a monitoring plan.

tasks.title: Reconstruct the timeline of a suspicious file transfer from packet captures and flow records and record the evidence with timestamps
Run a hypothesis-driven hunt for data exfiltration over DNS in a week of logs and report the hosts and evidence that support or refute it
Lead a scored incident response for a compromised branch router, choosing containment, evidence preservation and communication steps under time pressure
